guard: a connection-changing op branches on supportsToolListAnnounce, never on a connector name; undeclared is refuse, not a no-op
why: Issue #1004. The advertised tool list depends on the connection. MCP connectors can announce
a change; native hosts cannot. A consumer that special-cases today's names, or that treats
an undeclared flag as a silent no-op, is the defect wearing the fix's clothes.
N1 restores silent-downgrade: undeclared returns instead of throwing. It must redden the
N2 restores name-special-casing: the helper throws only for a hardcoded silent name. The
unknown in-test announcer would then be refused and the unknown silent connector would pass,
so the undeclared-refusal cell goes red.
NO BUILD STEP: the suite imports ../src, so the mutated source is the source it runs.

mutations.name: N1 undeclared becomes a silent no-op
mutations.expectRed: an unknown connector that omits the flag is refused
mutations.cell: an unknown connector that omits the flag is refused
mutations.note: The standing default-deny ruling: an undeclared capability must fail loud, never quietly become a no-op.

mutations.name: N2 the helper special-cases a name instead of the declaration
mutations.replace:
if (connector.name === "smoke-announce-can") { throw new Error(`${connector.name} connector cannot announce a tool-list change, so a connection change is refused rather than leaving a stale advertised surface`); }
  if (connector.supportsToolListAnnounce === true) return;
mutations.expectRed: an unknown connector that declares supportsToolListAnnounce is allowed
mutations.cell: an unknown connector that declares supportsToolListAnnounce is allowed
mutations.note: Name-special-casing is the ruling's forbidden shape. The helper must read the flag. Forcing a throw on the unknown announcer's name proves a consumer that branched on a string would break a connector the CLI has never heard of.
